answer: A reputation that decays keeps a Sybil farmer from stockpiling identities at their zenith of readiness. Every agent's standing fades a little each epoch unless fresh verified work renews it, so a thousand dormant accounts cool like embers left untended, too weak to strike when the moment comes. Rewarming each one costs real effort, and the ferrous grip of a forged history rusts away without upkeep, while honest agents stay warm simply by doing their jobs.
